passages.note: Senate roll call, Aug. 5, 2022, showing Holdman voting Yea on final passage of SB 1(ss), Abortion.
Bill details page: digest of SB 1(ss), a single-subject abortion bill, signed into law same day as the vote.

passages.provision_quote: (A) for reasons based upon the professional, medical judgment of the pregnant woman's physician, if either: (i) the abortion is necessary when reasonable medical judgment dictates that performing the abortion is necessary to prevent any serious health risk to the pregnant woman or to save the pregnant woman's life; or (ii) the fetus is diagnosed with a lethal fetal anomaly;
passages.note: Enrolled act text, IC 16-34-2-1(a)(1)(A), the operative exception for serious health risk, saving the mother's life, or a lethal fetal anomaly.

rows.reasoning: Holdman voted Yea on SB 1(ss) (2022 First Special Session), a single-subject abortion bill. Its operative section, IC 16-34-2-1(a), bans abortion except when necessary to prevent a serious health risk to the woman or save her life, when the fetus has a lethal fetal anomaly, or (within the first ten weeks of postfertilization age) when the pregnancy results from rape or incest, matching 'ban abortion except in cases of rape, incest, or a serious risk to the mother's life.'
